record.notes: The first General-Purpose AI Code of Practice draft is excluded from the output catalogue: independent experts drafted it and the AI Office published it as facilitator. This does not meet the institute-authorship or own-work credit rule. The announcement-to-establishment interval counts from the Commission decision of 24 January 2024; earlier announcements of the AI Act's political agreement are not counted. POLITICO reported on 31 July 2026 that the Commission was hiring contract agents for two units of the Office, one for AI regulation and compliance and one for the risks of cutting-edge models, which had a combined staff of 71, and that it expected 40 jobs to open in the two units during 2027; this press report does not change the staff figure. The Office's call for tenders EC-CNECT/2025/OP/0032 of 10 July 2025 for technical support on general-purpose AI safety has a total budget of EUR 9m from the Digital Europe Programme, in six lots with maximum values of EUR 1.08m to EUR 2m and durations of 24 or 36 months. This is a procurement ceiling, not a funding record. POLITICO reported on 6 March 2024 that the MEP Dragoș Tudorache, citing conversations with Commission officials, said the Office's starting budget would be EUR 46.5m; a Commission spokesperson said its funding would be reallocated from the Digital Europe Programme but declined to give specifics. This press report is not a funding record. The same report said that a Commission spokesperson had put the Office's planned total staff at 98, two of them working at the European Data Protection Supervisor, with 18 coming from other Commission units and 80 hired externally as contract staff or seconded national experts; this press report does not change the staff figure.

testing_capacity.notes: Testing reported, 2025-07-17: the AI Office ran the agentic evaluations for the cybersecurity strand of the network's joint testing. External evaluation support was procured under EC-CNECT/2025/OP/0032: lots 1 to 5 (CBRN, cyber offence, loss of control, harmful manipulation and sociotechnical risks) include ad hoc evaluations of general-purpose AI models chosen by the AI Office, and lot 6 builds an agentic evaluation interface for it. The award notice (OJ S 249/2025, 26 December 2025) lists the contractors by lot: lot 1 FAR AI, SecureBio and SaferAI; lot 2 Capgemini Consulting, Wavestone and the Laboratoire national de métrologie et d'essais; lot 3 EquiStamp, Model Evaluation and Threat Research and Epoch Artificial Intelligence; lot 4 EquiStamp, Clarity AI Research and the Centre pour la Sécurité de l'IA; lot 5 Technopolis Consulting Group Belgium, WIK-Consult and TNO; lot 6 the French ministry responsible for the budget and the Laboratoire national de métrologie et d'essais.

legal_power.conditions: Only for an evaluation under Article 92(1), which the AI Office conducts after consulting the Board, to assess a provider's compliance where information gathered under Article 91 is insufficient or to investigate systemic risks at Union level of general-purpose AI models with systemic risk; the request states its legal basis, purpose and reasons and the period for access, and the provider must provide the access requested.

model_access.notes: Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2026/1755 sets the arrangements: the access 'shall be appropriate to the objectives of the evaluation' and may include access through APIs, internal access, source code and model weights. The network joint testing used open-weight models. Signing the general-purpose AI Code of Practice is not counted as an access agreement. The tender specifications make the contractor responsible for 'the API costs associated with the GPAI model' and say 'Where not feasible, the AI Office shall aim to provide the required access.'

claims.text: The Commission announced the AI Office's first job opportunities.
The Commission decision establishing it assigns it developing tools, methodologies and benchmarks for evaluating the capabilities of general-purpose AI models.
The Commission decision establishing it assigns it investigating possible infringements of the rules on general-purpose AI models and systems.
The Commission decision establishing it assigns it supporting the implementation of the rules on prohibited AI practices and high-risk AI systems, in coordination with sectoral bodies.
The Commission decision establishing it assigns it monitoring the emergence of unforeseen risks from general-purpose AI models.
Under the AI Act, relevant information about serious incidents is to be reported to it without undue delay.
The Commission decision establishing it assigns it contributing to the Commission's international cooperation on AI with third countries and international organisations.
The Commission says it was one of the three network members that ran the agentic evaluations for the cybersecurity strand.
The Commission says it oversees the AI Pact, which allows businesses to engage with the Commission and other stakeholders to share best practices and join activities.

The Commission decision establishing it assigns it supporting the accelerated development, roll-out and use of trustworthy AI systems that contribute to the Union's competitiveness and economic growth.
The consolidated AI Act makes it responsible for conformity assessments and tests of the high-risk AI systems referred to in that article that are subject to third-party conformity assessment.

The Commission says the GenAI4EU initiative, one of those through which the AI Office supports innovators, contributes to novel use cases and emerging applications in 14 industrial sectors and the public sector.
The AI Act assigns it providing the secretariat for the Board, convening the Board's meetings at the Chair's request and preparing the agenda.
The Commission's announcement of the AI Office says it will conduct testing and evaluation of general-purpose AI models.
The Commission's answer says the AI Office has held numerous technical meetings with Anthropic to support implementation of the Code.
The AI Act assigns it developing a questionnaire template, including through an automated tool, to help deployers comply with their obligations under that article in a simplified manner.
The International Network's joint testing report says the EU AI Office, with UK AISI and Australia, ran evaluations on two open-source models.
The Commission says it has already started to use its enforcement powers under the AI Act, with requests for information sent to several companies to make sure they comply with their obligations.
The Commission says the AI Office monitors model capabilities.
The AI Act empowers the AI Office to establish a Union-level AI regulatory sandbox for systems covered by Article 75(1).

excerpts.text: The EU's executive confirmed Friday that it is seeking contract agents for two units within the two-year-old Artificial Intelligence Office

Both units currently have a combined staff of 71 people. The Commission expects 40 jobs to open up in both units over the course of 2027.
